theory Finite_Subject_Selection
  imports Finite_Derived_Observations
begin

section \<open>Required observations are evaluated on the actual mapped subjects\<close>

definition finite_requirement_scope where
  "finite_requirement_scope Fs Ws R \<longleftrightarrow>
    fimage fst R |\<subseteq>| Fs \<and> fimage snd R |\<subseteq>| Ws"

definition subject_requirements_hold where
  "subject_requirements_hold U W R P s \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<forall>(f,w)\<in>fset R. P (U f) s (W w))"

definition finite_subject_selection where
  "finite_subject_selection Cs Fs Ws C U W R P=
    (if finite_requirement_scope Fs Ws R
     then Some (ffilter (\<lambda>c. subject_requirements_hold U W R P (C c)) Cs)
     else None)"

theorem finite_subject_selection_formed:
  "finite_subject_selection Cs Fs Ws C U W R P\<noteq>None \<longleftrightarrow>
    finite_requirement_scope Fs Ws R"
  by (simp add: finite_subject_selection_def)

theorem finite_subject_selection_exact:
  assumes selected: "finite_subject_selection Cs Fs Ws C U W R P=Some A"
  shows "c |\<in>| A \<longleftrightarrow>
    c |\<in>| Cs \<and> subject_requirements_hold U W R P (C c)"
  using selected by (auto simp: finite_subject_selection_def split: if_splits)

theorem finite_subject_selection_uses_derived_observations:
  assumes scope: "finite_requirement_scope Fs Ws R"
  shows "finite_subject_selection Cs Fs Ws C U W R P=
    Some (ffilter (\<lambda>c. \<forall>(f,w)\<in>fset R.
      (f,c,w) |\<in>| finite_derived_observations
        (fimage (\<lambda>c. (c,C c)) Cs) (fimage (\<lambda>f. (f,U f)) Fs)
        (fimage (\<lambda>w. (w,W w)) Ws) P) Cs)"
proof -
  have indices: "f |\<in>| Fs \<and> w |\<in>| Ws" if "(f,w) |\<in>| R" for f w
    using scope that by (auto simp: finite_requirement_scope_def)
  show ?thesis
    unfolding finite_subject_selection_def if_P[OF scope]
    by (rule arg_cong[where f=Some], rule fset_eqI)
      (auto simp: subject_requirements_hold_def finite_derived_observation_on_function_graphs
        dest: indices)
qed

theorem finite_subject_selection_requirement_mono:
  assumes smaller: "R |\<subseteq>| S"
    and first: "finite_subject_selection Cs Fs Ws C U W R P=Some A"
    and second: "finite_subject_selection Cs Fs Ws C U W S P=Some B"
  shows "B |\<subseteq>| A"
  using smaller by (auto simp: fsubset_iff finite_subject_selection_exact[OF first]
    finite_subject_selection_exact[OF second] subject_requirements_hold_def)

theorem finite_subject_selection_at_subject:
  assumes selected: "finite_subject_selection Cs Fs Ws C U W R P=Some A"
    and subject: "c |\<in>| Cs" "C c=s"
  shows "c |\<in>| A \<longleftrightarrow> (\<forall>(f,w)\<in>fset R. P (U f) s (W w))"
  by (simp only: finite_subject_selection_exact[OF selected] subject
    subject_requirements_hold_def; simp)

text \<open>
  This operation accepts subject and operation maps, the independently required
  observations, and their actual predicate. It computes satisfaction at those
  subjects; no observation table is an input. Its exact equation identifies the
  result with the existing derived-observation calculation.

  An out-of-scope requirement fails instead of disappearing from the filter.
  A formed scope with no eligible candidate returns an empty set. The actual
  client must establish its predicate's condition contract and declared subject
  domain; arbitrary descriptions or callbacks supply no such guarantee.
\<close>

end

"""Execute the actual-source counterexample to identifying a program by its domain."""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import json

import check_reasoning
import investigate
import machine_reports
import proved_code


def program(engine, inputs):
    code = 'use ' + investigate.ml_string(str(engine)) + ';\n'
    code += 'structure N = Requirement_Source_Boundary;\n'
    code += check_reasoning.SCALAR_JSON_PRELUDE
    code += r'''
fun jinstruction _ = raise Fail "The proved source-boundary controls contain no instructions";
fun jplan NONE = "null"
  | jplan (SOME (ds,(next,instructions))) =
    "{\"entries\":" ^ jlist jnat ds ^ ",\"next\":" ^ jnat next ^
    ",\"instructions\":" ^ jlist jinstruction instructions ^ "}";
fun emit (i,hasClause) =
  let val (domain,(plan,(blueprint,installed))) = N.requirement_source_boundary_report hasClause
  in print ("REQUIREMENT_SOURCE_BOUNDARY " ^ Int.toString i ^
    " {\"source_has_clause\":" ^ Bool.toString hasClause ^ ",\"domain\":" ^ jlist jnat domain ^
    ",\"checked_plan\":" ^ jplan plan ^ ",\"blueprint_admitted\":" ^ Bool.toString blueprint ^
    ",\"installed_guard_on_empty_payload\":" ^ Bool.toString installed ^ "}\n") end;
'''
    code += 'val () = List.app emit ' + investigate.ml_list(
        list(enumerate(inputs['clause_presence'])),
        lambda row: '(' + str(row[0]) + ',' + ('true' if row[1] else 'false') + ')') + ';\n'
    return code


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    for name in ['proof', 'poly', 'project', 'output']:
        parser.add_argument('--' + name, type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    def assess(inputs, raw):
        path = args.output / 'results.log'
        assert path.read_text() == raw
        reports = list(machine_reports.reports(path))
        assert [r['tag'] for r in reports] == ['REQUIREMENT_SOURCE_BOUNDARY'] * 2
        assert [r['indices'] for r in reports] == [[0], [1]]
        assert [r['value']['source_has_clause'] for r in reports] == inputs['clause_presence']
        return {'complete_reports': reports, 'reproduction_boundary': machine_reports.boundary(path),
                'boundary': 'The input chooses whether the explicit ordinary source program contains its clause. '
                            'All observations are calculated on that actual program under the proved report equation. '
                            'This launcher checks complete serialization and retains the results.'}

    receipt = proved_code.checked_execution(
        args.proof, args.poly, args.output, required_theories=['Factor_Requirement_Source_Boundary'],
        inputs={'clause_presence': [False, True]}, input_paths=[Path(__file__)],
        program=program, assess=assess, project=args.project.resolve(),
        question='Can equal source domains and accepted plans identify the installed predicates meaning?',
        boundary='The two complete ordinary programs share a domain and blueprint but have different native meanings.')
    print(json.dumps({'status': receipt['status'], 'error': receipt.get('error'),
                      'reports': receipt.get('assessment', {}).get('complete_reports')}))
    return int(receipt['status'] != 'accepted')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())
